turn_text: Hey, it's great to be with you and your listeners.

I want to begin with questions that I know are of importance to you and I'll follow up the first specific question with a couple of local aspects of that. Under the administration of President Trump, the Environmental Protection Agency and other governmental bodies have sought to weaken protections for public lands and expand commercial exploitation of non-renewable resources in fragile environments. I'd like to know how you and other legislators respond to these trends.

Well I think what this has forced us to do is to get even more proactive about speaking out about our public lands in our state about really getting focused on the special places that deserve additional layers of protection and to do the kind of homework that it requires to put a community-based coalition together and to develop plans to protect those special places. And if there is a silver lining to the hostility that the Trump administration has brought to resources, to outdoor resources, then our environment generally, it's that I think it is forcing many communities to think about what's really near and dear to them and how they're going to work to protect those resources long-term.

turn_text: I'd like to turn our attention south now. Well having met with some of these families traveling north and I want to be careful about the the words we use because these are not immigrants these are largely refugees these are people who are in large measure hungry and scared because central america has so destabilized in in the last several years and i think that the policy in particular a separating families of tearing two-year-olds and three-year-olds and ten-year-olds away from mothers and fathers is has to be one of the most morally bankrupt decisions that any president of this country has ever made. It really worries me that this is going on at such high levels in this country. And I think it's also important to realize that if the president were serious about preventing this, he would be engaged with the leaders of those nations of Guatemala, of Honduras, of El Salvador to try and stabilize the region there. Because the reason people are leaving is because it is so dangerous in that region right now. And unfortunately, the president enjoys the issue rather than engaging and trying to fix the underlying things that are causing this to occur in the first place.
